h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: With edge 3 already an identity, a skip on edge 5 adds redundant identity while removing the deep path's final transform, so it hurts more.
Parallel identity routes into node 3 substitute for each other, so a second skip adds no new signal and dilutes the learned contribution.
A skip on edge 3 complements a conv-terminated deep path to form a clean residual block, the motif of top NAS-Bench-201 cells.
When edge 3 already supplies a conv path into node 3, a pooling branch on edge 4 replaces less needed capacity and hurts less.
With edge 4 removed, node 3 has fewer incoming paths, so a conv on edge 3 adds a larger share of the cell's learned output.
Edge 2 only matters if node 1 carries signal; the contrast includes edge 0 = none where node 1 is zero, and stacked convs compound, so the edge-2 conv gains more when edge 0 is a conv.
Features from an edge-0 conv are exploited by a learned edge-4 transform into node 3, whereas when edge 4 is none or parameter-free node 1's contribution to the output is weaker.
A conv on edge 1 keeps learned features flowing into node 2, so replacing edge 2 with a pool costs less.
With edge 2 removed, edge 1 is node 2's sole input, so its operation fully determines node 2's features and a conv there matters more.
Removing edge 3 when edge 5 is already gone leaves node 3 fed only by edge 4, so path removal compounds and hurts much more.
